summary: Defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module covering ATM-specific accounting information that can be collected for connections on ATM networks, such as for billing or usage tracking.

eli5.summary: If a network charges by use, someone has to count it. This document defines the standard counters for keeping track of how much each ATM connection was used.

questions: how to collect accounting data for atm connections
what is the atm accounting mib
what accounting data can an atm switch collect
what is a subtree list tuple in snmp
subtitle: A menu of per-connection usage items that an ATM switch can record for billing and tracking.

tldr.problem: Operators of ATM networks need to record how each connection was used, and the data must be described the same way on every vendor's switch.
tldr.mechanism: The MIB module defines 33 accounting items under one subtree, such as connection type, VPI, VCI, calling and called party, timestamps and cell counters. An administrator picks the items to collect as a (subtree, list) tuple.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard, not obsoleted. It supplies the vocabulary for accounting records while RFC 2513 controls how they are collected and stored.

today: RFC 2512 is a Proposed Standard from February 1999 and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is meant to be used with RFC 2513.

sections.title: Introduction and Purpose
sections.content:
RFC 2512 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for ATM-specific accounting information: data that can be collected for connections on ATM networks. It is a companion to RFC 2513, which defines, independently of the network type, how selected accounting data is collected and stored into files for later retrieval by a file transfer protocol.

The MIB module is named ATM-ACCOUNTING-INFORMATION-MIB and sits at mib-2 59. It was written by the IETF AToM MIB Working Group. Like the other modules in this family it is written in SMIv2, and the document includes the standard description of the SNMP Management Framework.
sections.eli5: This document is the list of facts a switch can jot down about each ATM connection. A sister document explains how to save the notes.

sections.title: How Items Are Selected
sections.content:
In RFC 2513 the items of accounting data are specified as a set of objects. The administrator picks which objects with one or more (subtree, list) tuples, and the set collected is the union of the subsets from each tuple.

  • The subtree is an OBJECT IDENTIFIER. Every object in the subset is named by that value plus one more sub-identifier.
  • The list is an OCTET STRING. If its N-th bit is set, the subset contains the object named by appending N to the subtree.

RFC 2512 supplies such a subtree: atmAcctngDataObjects. A tuple using it as the subtree selects which ATM items go into each record.

All the objects here have a MAX-ACCESS of not-accessible. They are not meant to be read or written with SNMP. They only define the syntax and meaning of values inside an accounting record.
sections.eli5: It is like a checklist with numbered boxes. You tick the boxes for the facts you want, and the switch writes down just those for every connection.

sections.title: Identity and Timing Items
sections.content:
The accounting objects are interpreted for one connection on one interface. Several of them say what the connection is and who was involved.

  • atmAcctngConnectionType takes one of ten values: pvc, pvp, svcIncoming, svcOutgoing, svpIncoming, svpOutgoing, spvcInitiator, spvcTarget, spvpInitiator and spvpTarget.
  • atmAcctngCastType says whether the connection is point-to-point or point-to-multipoint.
  • atmAcctngIfName and atmAcctngIfAlias name the interface. The name must match ifName when the agent supports it, and the alias stays across agent reboots.
  • atmAcctngVpi is 0 to 4095 and atmAcctngVci is 0 to 65535.
  • atmAcctngCallingParty, atmAcctngCalledParty, atmAcctngCallReference and the two sub-address objects are the zero-length string when unknown, for example on a PVC.

atmAcctngStartTime is when the connection was established and atmAcctngCollectionTime is when the record was collected. atmAcctngCollectMode gives the reason for collection: onRelease, periodically or onCommand. atmAcctngReleaseCause holds the cause code from the Release message of a released SVC, and is zero otherwise.
sections.eli5: These items say what kind of connection it was, which doors it used, who called whom, and when the notes were taken.

sections.title: Usage Counters and Traffic Descriptors
sections.content:
The usage items are 64-bit counters kept by the switch for the connection:

  • atmAcctngTransmittedCells and atmAcctngReceivedCells, which include OAM cells.
  • atmAcctngTransmittedClp0Cells and atmAcctngReceivedClp0Cells, which count only cells with CLP=0, again including OAM cells.

atmAcctngServiceCategory is one of other, cbr, vbrRt, vbrNrt, abr, ubr or unknown.

For each direction there is a traffic descriptor type, an OBJECT IDENTIFIER defined in RFC 1695 and its successors, plus five parameter objects, each from 0 to 2147483647. What each parameter means depends on the descriptor type.
sections.eli5: The counters are tally marks for how many small data packets (cells) went each way. The descriptors record the speed rules the connection was promised.

sections.title: The Record Checksum
sections.content:
The last object, atmAcctngRecordCrc16, is a 2-octet CRC-16 checksum (as defined by ISO 3309 (HDLC) and/or ITU X.25) calculated over the accounting record that contains it.

The way it is calculated depends on how the record is encoded, but the typical method is: start with the all-zeros string, remember where those zeros sit, generate the record, compute the checksum over the whole connection record, then overwrite the zeros with the result.
sections.eli5: It is a seal on the page. If someone scribbles on the record later, the seal no longer matches.

sections.title: Security and IANA Notes
sections.content:
The data items are only accessible through a collected accounting file. After collection, the accounting data should be protected against modification or unauthorized deletion.

The IANA section says that, prior to publication as an RFC, IANA is requested to make a suitable OBJECT IDENTIFIER assignment.
sections.eli5: Once the notes are written down, keep them safe so nobody changes the bill.
